## What families will get: a receipt that proves the payment {#families}

<span class="kicker">For school owners and directors</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card"><strong>A receipt they keep</strong>For every payment and refund, a receipt signed with your school's key: the amount, the date, your school, and a fingerprint of the entry in your books. No name or email inside.</div>
<div class="card card--green"><strong>Anyone can check it</strong>A family, their CPA or an auditor checks it with a free, open verifier. If your books are later edited, the receipt no longer matches.</div>
<div class="card card--ink"><strong>What it doesn't do yet</strong>It doesn't prove Stripe moved the money (daily matching is next), and it isn't an itemised, per-child receipt for a state program (planned).</div>
</div>

<p class="fine">Released in tfd 0.10.0 on 7 November 2026. No school issues these receipts yet, and no state program has accepted them; the first school pilot is next. Check your program's own receipt rules with your CPA.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `packages/atm/README.md`, "Receipts and seals (new in 0.10.0)" (the receipt holds school, the family's timeline key, the event id, type, time and date, amount, currency, Stripe id, and `event_hash`; "No name or email"; and "Not built: an itemised receipt... a proof of payment with no items, tax or student"); `docs/business/business-plan.md` §3 (released 2026-11-07, not yet issued by any school; daily Stripe matching milestone 3); `packages/atm/ROADMAP.md` milestone 1 ("a receipt does not prove Stripe moved the money"). Itemised receipts for state programs: compliance packs in `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §4, not built. State rules: `docs/business/market-research.md` §4 and §5 (check each program's rules from primary sources). AGENTS.md "Claims": say tfd signs receipts, not that families use them, until a school issues real receipts.
:::

## What a school would pay {#school-cost}

<span class="kicker">Sizing · illustrative</span>

<div class="cards">
<div class="card"><span class="big">≈ 7</span>ledger events a family makes in a month</div>
<div class="card card--green"><span class="big">≈ 140</span>families covered by the Free plan's 1,000 events. A 50-family school makes about 350.</div>
<div class="card card--ink"><span class="big">Half</span>the price for verified non-profits and co-ops: Starter $15, Pro $39, Witnessed $79</div>
</div>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--quiet"><strong>Running over never stops the books</strong>Limits are soft. Payments still book and receipts are still signed; after two months over, you're asked to move up a plan. Nothing is billed automatically.</div>
<div class="card card--quiet"><strong>Billing you can read</strong>A full refund within 30 days of the first paid charge, cancel in two clicks, change plans any time, onboarding included.</div>
</div>

<p class="assume-note"><span class="tag tag--assume">Assumption</span> The events-per-family figure comes from one test family; prices and policies are drafts to test with design-partner schools.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/business/business-plan.md` §8 ("A family makes about 7 events a month, so Free's 1,000 events covers about 140 families"); `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §5 rule 3 ("A school with about 50 families makes about 350 events a month, and Free covers it"), §3 (the estimate is from one fixture family, `packages/atm/fixtures/vibes-year`; replace with real data), §4 (soft limits; after two months over, asked to move up; Platform alone pays for events), §4a (billing policies: 30-day refund, two-click cancel, plan changes any time, onboarding included, export before and after cancelling), §4b (non-profit and co-op prices; verified 501(c) or cooperative). Credits running out: §5 rule 1 (payments still book, receipts still self-signed; only Rifo and new witness signatures pause).
:::

## Free to self-host, or let Trifold host it {#self-host-or-hosted}

<span class="kicker">Your choice</span>

<div class="cards cards--2">
<div class="card card--green"><strong>Community: run tfd yourself, $0</strong>
<ul>
<li>The whole engine and <code>tfd</code> CLI, for your own books</li>
<li>Self-signed receipts and seals, checkable with the open verifier</li>
<li>Source-available (FSL-1.1-ALv2); each release becomes Apache-2.0 two years after it ships</li>
<li>For technical schools and developers</li>
</ul></div>
<div class="card"><strong>Hosted Trifold <span class="tag tag--next">Next</span></strong>
<ul>
<li>Free plan: hosted books and signed receipts, no server to run</li>
<li>Paid plans for automation, teams, Rifo and, once it ships, Trifold as witness</li>
<li>Early access for design-partner schools; nothing hosted is live yet</li>
</ul></div>
</div>

<p class="fine">A school's self-signed receipts are "verifiable with the open verifier". Only records Trifold itself countersigns will say "Witnessed by Trifold".</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §1 (the rule) and §4 (Community: the whole engine and CLI, self-signed receipts and seals; Free hosted), §8 (FSL: free to use, modify and self-host for your own books; Apache-2.0 two years after each release); `docs/business/business-plan.md` §3 (hosted service not built); `TRADEMARKS.md`, "Witnessed by Trifold" (self-hosted receipts may say "verifiable with the open verifier", not "witnessed"). CTA wording "early access": `docs/website/decisions.md`.
:::

## Your books are yours {#your-data}

<span class="kicker">Data ownership</span>

<ul class="ticks">
<li>Export everything, in open formats, before and after you cancel. Export is never behind a paywall.</li>
<li>Erasure and privacy tools are never behind a paywall either.</li>
<li>Personal data stays out of signed receipts: no names or emails in them.</li>
<li>Verification is free for anyone, forever: the receipt format and verifier are Apache-2.0.</li>
<li>If you work with a bookkeeping firm and later leave it, your ledger comes with you.</li>
</ul>

<p class="fine">Student data: obligations (FERPA, state privacy laws) are checked per school type. How erasure works without breaking receipts is an owner decision still to make before schools issue receipts.</p>

::: {.notes}
Sources: `docs/business/pricing-strategy.md` §2 ("Never paywall": verification, data export, erasure and privacy tools, correctness and security fixes, the receipt and seal specs) and §4a ("Data on leaving: export everything, in open formats, before and after cancelling"); `docs/brand/trifold-brand-and-messaging.md` website outline ("data ownership: export to Parquet or hledger at any time"); `packages/atm/README.md` (no name or email in a receipt); `docs/business/business-plan.md` §10 (student data checked per school type; erasure-breaks-receipts owner decision); `packages/atm/ROADMAP.md` milestone 1 (erasure must not rewrite events: owner decision before release); `docs/business/go-to-market.md` §5 (a client can move with its ledger intact). AGENTS.md: verifier and format Apache-2.0.
:::

<span class="kicker">Next step</span>

<div class="cards">
